get.summary: Get option ordering data for all items in an LDS Session Part.

parameters.name: ldssession_id
parameters.description: UUID for LDSSession to add/replace variables for

parameters.name: question_index_pattern
parameters.description: A regular expression that matches a given "Question Index".  "Full" Questions Index strings are in the form `m1.s2.i3.q4` (and "relative" index values drop the `m#.` at the front).  As a regular expression, both full and partial matches are acceptable (including "full" and "relative" question indexes).  It shouldn't matter in most cases, but note that `.` is a meta-character in regular expressions, so you might want to escape it in the format `\.`.  Also note that `\d+` can be a handy shortcut to match the numbers that appears in the index strings.

200.description: Summary of requested LDSSession and LDSSessionPart with all Question Options Order information for the LDSSessionpart.

get.summary: Search for LDS Sessions that have a specific options order for a given question.
get.description:
Notes on `question_responses` format:
* Drag & Drop: Each pair is in the format `[<option_num>, <label_num>]`
* Category Drag & Drop: Each response chosen by the candidate/user is a triplet in the
    form `<option_num>, <category_num>-<label_num>` where:

      - `option_num` = ID number from the list of draggable items.
      - `category_num` = ID number of the category (column) an item was dragged to.
      - `label_num` = ID number of the label (drop zone) inside that category (column).

parameters.name: options_order_pattern
parameters.description: A regular expression that matches the "options order" string for each item/question that is shown to a user.  (The first time a user views each item, the questions in that item are prepared, including if the questions include randomized option order, and saves it in the database.)  The format of the values for a simple MCSA or MCMA with four options would appear as `[1, 2, 3, 4]` if `random_order=false` is specified (or something like `[2, 1, 4, 3]` if randomization is enabled on that question). Matrix-style questions will appear like `[[2, 1, 4, 3], [3, 1, 2]]`.  Note that if you want to include `[` or `]` characters in your regular expression, then you need to escape them with a `\` like `\]` or `\[` (`[` and `]` are meta-characters that are used to define a "character class", so if you don't escape them, the regular expession syntax will give them special meaning, including requiring them to be in matched pairs.)  Also note that all regular expressions in this endpoint are processed by the database and therefore use the POSIX style of regular expressions.

parameters.name: question_index_pattern
parameters.description: A regular expression that matches a given "Question Index".  "Full" Questions Index strings are in the form `m1.s2.i3.q4` (and "relative" index values drop the `m#.` at the front).  As a regular expression, both full and partial matches are acceptable (including "full" and "relative" question indexes).  It shouldn't matter in most cases, but note that `.` is a meta-character in regular expressions, so you might want to escape it in the format `\.`.  Also note that `\d+` can be a handy shortcut to match the numbers that appears in the index strings.

parameters.name: part_name_pattern
parameters.description: A regular expression that matches against the Form Qualified Name (FQN) of the LDS Session Part a question appeared in.

parameters.name: from
parameters.description: Beginning time range to pull from (in `YYYY-MM-DD` format).  Note that records from the start of the date specified will be included.  The default is 30 days prior to the current day.  Also note that while it normally won't matter, technically, this is filtering against the time that a given question was queried by the LDS Frontend, not the session "schedule date" or other times.

parameters.name: to
parameters.description: Ending time range to pull from (in `YYYY-MM-DD` format).  Note that records through midnight at the end of the date specified will be included.  The default is the current day ("today").  Also note that while it normally won't matter, technically, this is filtering against the time that a given question was queried by the LDS Frontend, not the session "schedule date" or other times.
